questions.answer: DNA is transcribed into mRNA in the nucleus, and the mRNA is translated into a polypeptide at a ribosome in the cytoplasm.
questions.explanation: Scene s1 shows the one-way flow: transcription copies DNA into mRNA in the nucleus, then translation reads the mRNA at a ribosome to build the polypeptide chain.
questions.prompt: Outline the central dogma in one or two sentences, naming where transcription and translation happen.

questions.answer: A son has only one X chromosome, so the recessive h allele has no second allele to mask it and the trait shows; a daughter has a second X carrying H, which masks h, so she is a carrier without symptoms.
questions.explanation: Scene s4 makes the asymmetry explicit: sons receive their only X from their mother and a Y from their father, so there is no second X to mask a recessive allele; daughters receive an X from each parent.
questions.prompt: A carrier mother (X^H X^h) and a normal father (X^H Y) have children. Explain why a son who inherits X^h has haemophilia, while a daughter who inherits X^h usually does not.
